messages:
devon: FYI — support ticket #11234. Customer reports intermittent 401s and a retry storm after we merged the latest cross-sdk regen (TS & Python). Repro is a Next.js app using the new TS client 0.12.0-gen. Anyone seen auth regressions from the generator?

maria: Ugh, saw one flaky e2e yesterday in CI but assumed test setup. Details on the 401 pattern?

devon: Logs from the app show: first request returns 401, our client auto-retries immediately (no backoff) and spikes requests. Customer says it started after they upgraded the client.

kevin: Quick guess: the new generator accidentally made auth optional and moves token to a different header field name in the browser build. If Authorization header gets sent as "authorization" or as a param it might be stripped by some proxies/CORS.

anya: Also saw a change in generated retry middleware — it used to honor Retry-After and exponential backoff, new code does naive immediate retries x3. That would amplify a transient auth failure into a burst.

support-bot: Customer-provided repro steps:
1) Next.js app using fetch + @redwood/sdk-ts 0.12.0-gen
2) Server-side render and client hydration in same request path
3) Intermittent 401s, then a sequence of 3 identical requests within ~200ms
4) Auth is via ephemeral session cookie -> exchange to API token at runtime

devon: Customer included a minimal repro. Paste of failing fetch headers: 
```
fetch('/api/gen', {
  headers: {
    'authorization': 'Bearer xxxxxx' // lowercase header
  }
})
```

maria: That lowercase header could be fine but many CDNs normalize. If our generated client changed header casing or moved token to query param for SSR, that'll break auth in edge cases.

kevin: Can we confirm generator diff? I pulled the regen PR — looks like TS client swapped from setting `headers['Authorization']` to merging an `auth` object into fetch options: `...opts.auth`. That path ends up omitted in the browser bundle because our bundler shim drops unknown top-level fields.

anya: Repro locally: pinned older client (0.11.3) -> no 401s, retries respect Retry-After. Switch to 0.12.0-gen -> 401 + immediate retries.

ci-bot: CI flaky tests flagged: package@ts-client-e2e on linux-x64 failed 4/20 runs with 401-mismatch. Related to PR #4821 (client-regenerate-openapi).

devon: Short-term mitigation for the customer: downgrade to 0.11.3 or patch their app to set `headers['Authorization']` explicitly before calling client. Also we can push a hotfix to generator to preserve header behavior + backoff.

maria: I can draft a customer reply with both options. Support, please give guidance about downgrade steps and a rollback note.

support-bot: Suggested message: "We're seeing a regression in the regenerated TS client affecting auth header propagation and retry timing. Temporary options: pin to 0.11.3 or set the Authorization header explicitly on your requests. We're preparing a generator patch; ETA ~ 24 hours." :thumbsup:

kevin: For the fix: change generator template to always call `setHeader('Authorization', token)` rather than relying on merging `auth` object; revert the retry middleware to honor Retry-After and exponential backoff. I'll open a PR and tag @maria for review.

anya: I'll add an integration test in pipeline that runs a minimal SSR scenario against the packaged browser build to catch header bundling regressions. Add a flaky guard in CI to fail fast if 401 rate > 1%.

devon: Also record this in a changelog note — breaking behavior in regened clients for a minor bump is bad. Need to improve our regen release notes automation so we don't miss auth/backoff behavior changes.

maria: Thanks — please paste the PR here when it's up. I'll coordinate the customer comms and mark the ticket as high priority.

kevin: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/regen-fix-4821 (includes tests + rollback of retry policy).

devon: I'll ask SRE to monitor token-exchange endpoints for any surge while we roll the patch.

support-bot: Ticket updated: escalation -> eng-led fix. Customer advised to pin or set header.

anya: Follow-up action items: [kevin] submit generator patch, [maria] customer note, [ci-team] add SSR header test, [devon] monitor SRE metrics.

kevin: Will do, ETA PR merge in ~3h.

maria: Perfect. Closing the loop once merged and a new client release is published. :white_check_mark:
